project.title: Evaluating Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Factual Question Answering over a University Policy Corpus
project.research_question: RQ1: Does retrieval-augmented generation improve factual question answering accuracy over closed-book models on university policy documents? RQ2: Does passage retrieval reduce unsupported claims?
objectives: Evaluate answer correctness across 120 benchmark policy questions
Quantify reduction in unsupported factual assertions
Execute paired significance testing via McNemar test
project.claimed_contribution: A paired evaluation framework establishing that retrieval augmentation improves accuracy from 59.2% to 81.7% with p = 0.0000143.
project.methodology: We employ a within-question paired design using 120 benchmark questions, evenly distributed across academic regulations, course registration, financial assistance, and campus services. Each question was processed by the ResearchBuddy-Sim-7B-Instruct v1.0 model in two conditions: (1) Closed-book, and (2) RAG with top-5 passages retrieved via Embed-Sim-v1. Evaluation performed via human-style annotation with synthetic Cohen's kappa of 0.82. Paired discordant pairs evaluated using exact two-sided McNemar test.
project.dataset_or_materials: 120 curated university policy questions paired with official institutional documentation passages.
project.results: In the primary evaluation of answer-level correctness, the closed-book condition resulted in 71 correct answers (59.2%), while the RAG condition resulted in 98 correct answers (81.7%). The paired contingency table reveals that 65 questions were correct in both, 33 were correct only in RAG, 6 were correct only in closed-book, and 16 were incorrect in both. An exact two-sided McNemar test on the discordant pairs (33 vs 6) yields p = 0.0000143, indicating statistical significance. Unsupported claims fell from 52 of 120 (43.3%) to 24 of 120 (20.0%).
project.limitations: The findings are derived from synthetic data, a single model architecture, and a simplified retrieval pipeline.

cases.source_draft: We evaluated 120 questions across university policy domains. Closed-book got 71 correct (59.2%), RAG got 98 correct (81.7%). Contingency: 65 both correct, 33 RAG only, 6 closed only, 16 neither. McNemar p = 0.0000143. Unsupported claims: 52 (43.3%) closed-book down to 24 (20.0%) RAG. Cohen's kappa was 0.82.

Karpukhin, V., et al. (2020). Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering. EMNLP.

project.title: Deep Multi-Task Learning for Histopathological Phenotype Screening: Preliminary Pilot Study
project.research_question: Can multi-task CNN backbones achieve high diagnostic sensitivity on needle biopsy slides prior to large-scale prospective multi-center trial completion?
objectives: Develop a weakly supervised slide classification network
Assess pilot sensitivity on an initial single-center cohort of 50 patients
project.claimed_contribution: A multi-task histology screening pipeline demonstrating 84.2% pilot sensitivity with clear boundary identification for pending phase 2 trials.
project.methodology: We train a multi-task ResNet-50 network on 256x256 patch tiles extracted from whole slide images. Training employs cross-entropy loss with Adam optimization (learning rate 0.0001). Initial evaluation is conducted on a preliminary retrospective cohort of 50 patient biopsies from a single medical center.
project.dataset_or_materials: 50 retrospective whole-slide biopsy images curated from a single clinical site.
project.results: On the initial 50-patient pilot cohort, the network achieved a diagnostic sensitivity of 84.2% and specificity of 78.6%. Phase 2 multi-center validation on 500 prospective patients is currently underway and not yet completed.
project.limitations: Pilot study limited to a single medical center; multi-center prospective validation is pending.

cases.source_draft: Pilot cohort of 50 biopsies achieved 84.2% sensitivity and 78.6% specificity. Multi-center phase 2 trial on 500 patients has not been completed.

references.text: Campanella, G., et al. (2019). Clinical-grade computational pathology using weakly supervised deep learning on whole slide images. Nature Medicine.

project.title: Adaptive Hierarchical Routing for Distributed Edge Model Inference
project.research_question: How can dynamic priority queuing optimize tail latency in multi-tenant edge inferencing without violating strict memory budgets?
objectives: Formulate analytical queuing dynamics under Lyapunov drift optimization
Characterize theoretical memory bounds under heterogeneous packet arrivals
project.claimed_contribution: A theoretical routing framework with proven upper bounds on queue backlog and latency.
project.methodology: We formulate an analytical queuing model using Markov decision processes and Lyapunov drift optimization across 3 edge topologies. State space transitions are bounded by Lipschitz continuity over arrival distributions.
project.limitations: Theoretical formulation has not been deployed on physical hardware.

cases.source_draft: This paper presents a theoretical formulation of adaptive hierarchical routing for distributed edge inference. Physical experiments have not been conducted.

references.text: Neely, M. J. (2010). Stochastic Network Optimization with Application to Communication and Queueing Systems. Morgan & Claypool.

project.title: Equivariant Graph Neural Networks for Molecular Conformation and Ground-State Energy Approximation
project.research_question: Does enforcing SE(3) Lie group equivariance in message-passing neural networks improve ground-state molecular energy prediction over non-equivariant baselines?
objectives: Formulate an SE(3)-equivariant continuous message passing operator
Evaluate mean absolute energy prediction error on the QM9 molecular benchmark
Derive Lipschitz continuity bounds governing gradient stability
project.claimed_contribution: An SE(3)-equivariant architecture achieving a Mean Absolute Error of 0.018 eV on QM9 molecular ground-state energy prediction.
project.methodology: Let G = (V, E) denote a molecular graph where each node v in V possesses coordinates x_v in R^3 and atomic features h_v. We define an equivariant coordinate update operator mapping relative displacement vectors under radial filter functions W(||x_i - x_j||). Energy prediction is derived from a Hamiltonian potential function. Evaluated on the QM9 benchmark across 134,000 organic molecules.
project.dataset_or_materials: QM9 benchmark dataset consisting of 134,000 stable small organic molecules.
project.results: On the QM9 benchmark for ground-state internal energy (U_0), the proposed equivariant network achieved a Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of 0.018 eV, outperforming standard SchNet (0.042 eV) and non-equivariant DimeNet baselines.
project.limitations: Evaluated on small equilibrium molecules; computational scaling to macromolecular proteins requires further sparsification.

cases.source_draft: QM9 benchmark evaluation: proposed equivariant model achieved MAE of 0.018 eV compared to 0.042 eV for standard baselines. SE(3) equivariance preserved.

references.text: Satorras, V. G., et al. (2021). E(n) Equivariant Graph Neural Networks. ICML.

project.title: Neural and Lexical Paradigms in Modern Information Retrieval: A Comprehensive Survey
project.research_question: How do sparse lexical indices, dense vector representations, and multi-vector late-interaction architectures compare across retrieval effectiveness, index footprint, and latency?
objectives: Thematically categorize modern IR architectures into sparse, dense, and late-interaction paradigms
Synthesize cross-benchmark performance metrics and computational trade-offs
project.claimed_contribution: A systematic survey categorizing modern retrieval pipelines across 8 foundational paradigms with explicit memory and throughput trade-off surfaces.
project.methodology: A comparative analytical survey and meta-synthesis of published literature across 8 peer-reviewed retrieval architectures, evaluating algorithmic complexity, index storage requirements, and out-of-domain transfer on the BEIR benchmark.
project.limitations: Synthesizes published results from peer-reviewed literature and does not independently re-index terabyte-scale corpora.

project.title: Quantization-Aware Training for Edge Transformer Deployment
project.research_question: Can 8-bit integer quantization maintain inference accuracy in vision transformers without extensive full-precision retraining?
objectives: Evaluate post-training quantization vs quantization-aware training
Quantify top-1 accuracy on ImageNet-1K
project.claimed_contribution: An empirical benchmark of INT8 quantization for vision transformers with conflict identification.
project.methodology: We quantize a ViT-Base architecture using symmetric uniform INT8 quantization across weights and activations. Evaluation performed on ImageNet-1K validation set (50,000 images).
project.results: Accuracy was 91.2% in the final benchmark evaluation.
project.limitations: Tested only on vision transformers; recurrent models not evaluated.

cases.source_draft: Preliminary INT8 quantization experiments reported accuracy was 87.4% on the test subset.

project.title: Decoupled Cross-Attention Networks for High-Throughput Biomedical Signal Telemetry
project.research_question: How can multi-channel electroencephalogram (EEG) signals be decoded in real-time under severe computational and memory constraints?
objectives: Design a decoupled cross-attention pipeline for 64-channel EEG decoding
Benchmark latency and Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) improvements
Profile memory footprint across NVIDIA A100 and edge accelerators
project.claimed_contribution: A decoupled neural architecture improving SNR from 8.6 dB to 14.2 dB with a 12.4 ms inference latency.
project.methodology: We record 64-channel continuous EEG sampled at 500 Hz across 40 subjects under controlled cognitive workload paradigms. Bandpass filtering (0.5 to 100 Hz) and notch filtering (50 Hz) remove power-line interference. The neural architecture decouples spatial electrode embedding from temporal self-attention. Benchmark executions profile throughput across NVIDIA A100 and Jetson Orin hardware.
project.dataset_or_materials: 64-channel continuous EEG recordings sampled at 500 Hz from 40 healthy adult participants.
project.results: Across 40 subjects, the decoupled model enhanced average Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) from 8.6 dB in raw telemetry to 14.2 dB in decoded output. Median inference latency per 2-second epoch was 12.4 ms on the Jetson Orin, well within the 50 ms real-time telemetry threshold. Peak memory consumption was 186 MB.
project.limitations: Evaluated in controlled laboratory environments; motion artifacts in ambulatory subjects require adaptive filtering.

cases.source_draft:
Exhaustive Laboratory Telemetry Log:
Subject cohort: 40 participants, 64-channel EEG, 500 Hz sampling rate. Filtering: 0.5-100 Hz bandpass, 50 Hz notch. Decoupled cross-attention architecture tested across A100 and Jetson Orin edge accelerators. Results: SNR improved from 8.6 dB to 14.2 dB. Inference latency: 12.4 ms per 2-second window. Memory usage: 186 MB. Zero packet drop over 12 continuous test hours. Sensitivity profiling confirmed robustness against non-Gaussian physiological noise. Complete hyperparameter logs: learning rate 0.0003, weight decay 0.01, cosine decay with 10-epoch warmup, batch size 64.

project.title: Federated Optimization with Dynamic Gradient Pruning for Resource-Constrained Telemetry
project.research_question: Can dynamic magnitude-based gradient pruning reduce uplink bandwidth in federated learning without causing model divergence?
objectives: Propose a local thresholding heuristic for client gradient pruning
Analyze convergence conditions on non-IID client distributions
project.claimed_contribution: A conceptual framework demonstrating convergence bounds for 90% pruned federated gradients.
project.methodology: We formulate a localized pruning threshold tau_i dynamically adapted to client local gradient norms. Pruned gradients are transmitted to a central parameter server using FedAvg aggregation.
project.limitations: Exploratory mathematical analysis; physical wireless deployment is ongoing.

cases.source_draft: Brief project seed note: We explore client gradient pruning in federated optimization. Physical testbed trials are pending.

project.title: Synthetic Evaluation Framework for End-to-End Latency in SDN-Governed Edge Topologies
project.research_question: How does flow-table caching affect tail packet latency across simulated software-defined networking switches?
objectives: Simulate 10,000 synthetic packet flows across an OMNeT++ edge network model
Quantify queue delays and packet drop rates under synthetic burst traffic
project.claimed_contribution: A simulation study characterizing SDN flow-table eviction policies with explicit synthetic modeling caveats.
project.methodology: A discrete-event simulation model implemented in OMNeT++ with INET framework. The simulation executes 10,000 synthetic packet flows across a 5-node topology. All traffic generation follows a synthetic Pareto distribution.
project.dataset_or_materials: OMNeT++ simulation configuration files and 10,000 synthetic packet event traces.
project.results: Under synthetic Pareto traffic, simulated throughput reached 942 Mbps with a mean synthetic queue delay of 4.2 ms across 10,000 simulated packets.
project.limitations: All packet traces, queue latencies, and drop rates are derived from an OMNeT++ discrete-event simulation model and do not represent physical hardware telemetry.

cases.source_draft: Simulated evaluation: 10,000 synthetic packets in OMNeT++. Simulated throughput: 942 Mbps, synthetic queue delay: 4.2 ms. Synthetic modeling limitations apply.
